subject: Control-plane mesh instability after October private-node rollout — evidence and next steps
messages:
From: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@stellarneuro.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: recent private-node rollout — intermittent control-plane failures

Hi Maya,

We started seeing intermittent control-plane "mesh" disconnects in our staging VPC right after the private-node upgrade you pushed at 03:00 UTC this morning. Symptoms: a small window (~2–3 minutes) where agent heartbeats stop for ~40% of nodes, then reconverge; we also see elevated 502s to our inference endpoints for affected models.

I've attached the agent-side logs and a kv snapshot we pulled. Can your team advise whether anything in the October private-node package could cause transient leader election contention? We can reproduce the brief packet loss window reliably by replaying traffic.

Alejandra
Senior SRE, Stellar Neuro

Hi Alejandra,

Thanks for the quick heads-up and the artifacts — this is helpful. We're pulling the traces into an internal debug runbook now. Initial read: there are repeated TLS handshake timeouts between controllers during leader churn; could be exacerbated by a small window where certificate rotation and agent rejoin coincide.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@stellarneuro.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: recent private-node rollout — intermittent control-plane failures

Maya/Hannah — I pulled the log. Quick notes: repeated "leader not found" followed by TLS handshake error 1203 (peer cert invalid) around 03:02–03:05 UTC. The upgrade includes an optimized cert-renewal timing tweak; if rotation occurs while node reboots overlap, we can hit a transient window where controllers disagree on valid certs.

Mitigation we can try now (low-risk):
1) Disable the post-upgrade cert rotation task on your private controlplane (single CLI flag) and re-run the join flow. This will avoid a double-rotation race until we ship a patch.
2) If you prefer, we can trigger a controlled warm restart of controllers sequentially to force a clean leader election (we can coordinate ETA).

I'll prepare a small hotfix to widen the cert validity overlap window; Hannah I'll need help validating across qemu test harness and a small customer canary.

Marcus
Staff SWE, Runtime and Control Plane
Attachment: proposed-hotfix-diff.patch (text/plain, 12KB)

Please keep us posted on the hotfix timeline; if you can get a canary build by EOD that'd be ideal.

Subject: Re: recent private-node rollout — intermittent control-plane failures

Folks — I validated Marcus's repro locally on the qemu harness. The race happens when:
- node A rotates cert at t0
- node B reboots and presents old signed cert during t0..t0+30s
- controller comparison logic rejects B until it observes A's new cert claim

Patch approach: add a 90s overlap acceptance window for previous certs and ensure our KV gossip marks a provisional leader during rotation to reduce election churn. I'll cut a canary image (sha: canary-20281004-rotfix) and start a canary run against a trimmed replay.

ETA: canary build in ~5 hours, validated across two harness runs (~3–4 minutes each).

Hannah
SRE Lead, Runtime Reliability

Subject: Control-plane mesh follow-up and postmortem summary (SUP-7092)

Hi Alejandra and team —

Thank you again for partnering through the investigation. Quick summary and customer-facing mitigations: 

What happened:
- During the October private-node rollout, a cert rotation timing tweak combined with overlapping node restarts created a short window where some controllers rejected incoming peer certs and triggered leader election churn. This caused brief agent heartbeats to fail and a transient spike in 502s.

Impact:
- Staging environment: repeated short windows (~2–3 minutes) of elevated 502s, affecting ~40% of nodes in the cluster for each window. No data loss; KV consistency remained intact.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Disabled automated cert rotation in your staging controlplane during triage.
- Provided a hotfix canary (canary-20281004-rotfix).
- Recommended rolling patch procedure (attached) — you applied in staging on 2028-10-05 and observed normal reconvergence.

Permanent fix and timeline:
- We will ship a stable release with widened cert-overlap acceptance and provisional leader marking in the 2028-10-11 maintenance batch. Affected customers will receive detailed upgrade notes.

Action items for Stellar Neuro (what we did / ask of you):
- Keep cert-rotation disabled until you validate the stable release, or schedule Redwood to apply the release.
- We recommend a short canary run in your production replica set once we ship on Oct 11.

Artifacts attached: controlplane-trace-20281004.log, kv-snapshot-20281004.json; bridge recording (call-recording-20281004.mp3) is available on the drive link.

We've opened SUP-7092 to track the fix and will send a formal postmortem after the stable release is deployed. Please let me know if you'd like Redwood to coordinate the production canary.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
